file-description.file-description-heading: This file contains thermal insulation and material data for the Thermal Calculator application.
file-description-text: - Contains thermal conductivity values for various insulation materials
- Lists R-values for different material thicknesses
- Includes notes and warnings for correct application

log-changes: - Initial creation of thermal data library
- Added PIR, phenolic, mineral wool, glass mineral wool, masonry and timber materials

50mm-Thickness.notes: Standard PIR board for floors, walls and roofs.
50mm-Thickness.info: Suitable for warm and cold roof applications.
50mm-Thickness.warnings: Ensure VCL is used where required to avoid condensation risks.

60mm-Thickness.notes: Standard PIR board for floors, walls and roofs.
60mm-Thickness.info: Ground floor and suspended floor applications.
60mm-Thickness.warnings: Board must be tightly butted to avoid thermal bridging.

70mm-Thickness.notes: Standard PIR board for floors, walls and roofs.
70mm-Thickness.info: Good balance of thermal performance and thickness.
70mm-Thickness.warnings: Ensure correct fixing pattern is used.

75mm-Thickness.notes: Often used in roof rafter applications.
75mm-Thickness.info: High thermal performance in minimal thickness.
75mm-Thickness.warnings: Compression can reduce effective R-value if not installed flat.

80mm-Thickness.notes: Provides good thermal performance for roofs and floors.
80mm-Thickness.info: Suitable for achieving lower U-values in constrained spaces.
80mm-Thickness.warnings: Ensure correct fixings are used for the application.

90mm-Thickness.notes: High performance insulation for demanding applications.
90mm-Thickness.info: Helps achieve Part L compliance with single layer.
90mm-Thickness.warnings: Requires careful handling to avoid damage to board edges.

100mm-Thickness.notes: Maximum thickness in the GA4000 range.
100mm-Thickness.info: Provides excellent thermal performance for all applications.
100mm-Thickness.warnings: Heavyweight board requires careful handling and installation.

90mm-Thickness.notes: Specifically designed for cavity wall applications.
90mm-Thickness.info: Premium thermal performance for cavity walls.
90mm-Thickness.warnings: Must be installed with correct cavity wall ties.

115mm-Thickness.info: Suitable for meeting stringent U-value requirements.

140mm-Thickness.notes: Maximum thickness for cavity wall applications.

75mm-Thickness.notes: Cavity wall insulation with tongue and groove edges.
75mm-Thickness.info: Minimizes thermal bridging at board junctions.

90mm-Thickness.notes: Tongue and groove PIR for cavity wall systems.
90mm-Thickness.info: Designed for partial fill with 50mm air gap retained.
90mm-Thickness.warnings: Incorrect cavity tie spacing can lead to slumping.

115mm-Thickness.info: For use in applications requiring very low U-values.
115mm-Thickness.warnings: Requires correct detailing at wall junctions.

140mm-Thickness.notes: Maximum thickness available for cavity walls.
140mm-Thickness.info: Used for Passivhaus and ultra-low energy buildings.

25mm-Thickness.notes: Premium phenolic insulation for cavity walls.
25mm-Thickness.info: Offers better thermal performance than PIR.
25mm-Thickness.warnings: Requires careful handling due to rigid board properties.

50mm-Thickness.info: More efficient than equivalent thickness of PIR.

75mm-Thickness.info: Used where space is at a premium.

standard.info: Variable thickness material for cavity walls.
standard.warnings: Must be kept dry during storage and installation.

standard.info: Suitable for lofts and between timber joists.

standard.warnings: Must be protected from water during installation.

Outer-Leaf.notes: Typical clay brick for external walls.
Outer-Leaf.info: Standard value for U-value calculations per BR 443:2019.
Outer-Leaf.warnings: Thermal conductivity affected by moisture content.

Inner-Leaf.notes: Typical clay brick for internal walls.
Inner-Leaf.warnings: Thermal bridges at mortar joints not accounted for.

Dense-Aggregate.info: Used for structural applications and inner leaves.
Dense-Aggregate.warnings: Poor thermal performance requires additional insulation.

Lightweight-Aggregate.info: Better thermal performance than dense blocks.
Lightweight-Aggregate.warnings: Lower compressive strength than dense blocks.

standard.info: Denser wood with higher thermal conductivity.
standard.warnings: Less commonly used in thermal elements.
